# The README's first screen shows the engine and names who builds it

**No `good first issue` / `help wanted` label:** owned, and it has to merge before the copy lock (Sun 22 Nov 18:00 CET): npm freezes the README it shows at the v14 publish on Mon 23 Nov.

## Context

`README.md` is the first thing a visitor reads on two pages: the repository's page (3,305 stars) and the package's page on npm, where it sits at the very top. Engine 14 ships on Mon 23 Nov and sends strangers to both.

The operator's read on 20 Nov 2026: the new examples overview shows the component library and the engine well, the home's previews are fine, and the engine repository "does not make it clear at all"; "a couple of screenshots might already help"; the trade-off is that this is the only repository of the org with traction, "so it needs to describe our agent institution too". His argument for the change: the README "clearly did not convert". In the 14 days to 20 Nov, 55 outside accounts merged a pull request in the org's public repositories (GitHub search) while the repository gained 9 stars (stargazer dates); the stars of July to October were 28, 18, 22 and 20 a month.

## The Problem

Read on `dev` `5cb81df00a`, 20 Nov 2026, logged out, at 1440 × 900:

| What | Reading |
|---|---|
| Where the README starts on the repository page | 1.7 screens below the head |
| Its length | 10.4 screens, 2,872 words |
| Content images | 1, the film cover of v13.2 |
| The engine's paragraph | line 108 of 241, after the organism, the repository map and the deployment pitch |
| The first step, `npx neo-app@latest` | line 153 |
| Gantt, scheduler, task board | named nowhere; they are Engine 14's headline (#20874) |
| A link to the examples overview | none |
| The dated proof line | June 2026: "900+ merged PRs" in one repository. GitHub search for October across the org's public repositories (`org:neomjs is:public`): 1,211 merged pull requests, 200 of them Dependabot's, and 1,227 closed issues |
| "A Platform at Scale" | a snapshot of May 2026 |
| The repository's GitHub description | the organism-wide concise form |

A web engineer who follows an Engine 14 link reads "An agent institution" and scrolls four screens before a grid is mentioned. Nothing on the page shows one.

## The Architectural Reality

- `Design authority: "First-contact pages | Show the reader's task, a demonstrated benefit and a first step."` (`.agents/skills/neo-identity-update/references/framing-governance.md`, the claim gate) and `"Each repository's own metadata projects its own product — for neomjs/neo the Engine (OD-4 …); an organism-wide description there is drift."` (the same file, mirroring `learn/agentos/decisions/0018-neo-identity-source-of-truth-model.md` §2.3).
- The README's top is a member of the lead cluster: the label "an agent institution", then the ladder sentence (#21420). Both stay word for word.
- ADR 0018 §2.3 places the apex directly behind the label, "as the proof paragraph" (the operator's placement of 2026-10-16). This ticket puts the repository's own product between them on this one README, which changes that sentence of the record.
- The label leads the README "because findability is the job there" (#19811): answer engines list by category and read the most-indexed repository. The label therefore stays in the H1, in the second sentence and as the heading of the README's second part.
- The description: #18282's body (4 Sep) kept the organism sentence; ADR 0018 §2.3 as amended on 16 Oct (#19811) has `neomjs/neo`'s description describe the Engine. The live value is still the former.
- `test/playwright/unit/apps/portal/view/home/AudienceDoors.spec.mjs:126-133` reads `README.md` and asserts four strings: the class and namespace counts, `## Who This Is For`, `### 🤖 The Body — The Application Engine` and `npx neo-app@latest`.
- About 70 covers of v14 examples are hosted in `neomjs/pages` (`resources_pub/website/examples/devmode/*-14.jpg`, 1280 × 720, retaken by the tile recipe of #21332). The README already loads its film cover from that repository.
- The overview's 21 groups in five bands stand in `apps/portal/view/examples/MainContainer.mjs:78-98`; a group's route is `https://neomjs.com/#/examples/<group>`. On the live 13.4 site such a route opens the examples section, so the links hold before the release deploy.

## The Fix

One pull request, most of it a re-order of existing text:

1. **First screen.** The H1 becomes "An application engine built by an agent institution". Two sentences lead: what the engine is, then who builds it, with the institution said by its properties (named AI maintainers from rival labs, memory, cross-family review, one human at the merge gate). A record line gives October's numbers with their searches. Three rows of doors follow, one per audience: build (with the install command), run a team, contribute. Then one large picture of DevIndex, linked to the live app (the operator's pick on 20 Nov: 50,000 real GitHub contributors streamed into one grid), and below it a table of six linked covers with a one-line caption each: grid, Gantt, scheduler, task board, calendar, dock layouts.
2. **Second screen, "The Engine".** The Body's paragraphs move up. A list says what ships: Apps and the overview's five bands, every group linked to its page. Quickstart, the runtime's threads and the possession interface follow.
3. **Then the lead cluster, whole and in its order,** opens the README's second part: the label as heading, the ladder sentence, the apex paragraphs with the film. The repository map, the maintainer table, the deployment section, the Brain, "Who This Is For" and "Read Next" follow, unchanged in substance.
4. **Facts.** The record, the proof line and the deployment section carry the 30 days to 20 Nov 2026 for the public repositories (the operator's window, with both dates so it ages well), with the outside contributors of that window and the queries in the pull request.
5. **Cuts.** "A Platform at Scale" goes (its numbers live in the Codebase Overview, which "Read Next" links). The "Architecture" heading goes; its two lists move into the Engine and Brain sections.
6. **The record.** ADR 0018 §2.3 gains one sentence on this README's order, with its date in the Amended row. The operator's merge confirms it, as on #21420.
7. **The spec** follows the changed heading.
8. **Out of tree.** The repository's description takes the Engine's projection from `package.json` (`gh repo edit`); the pull request lists it before and after.

## Decision Record impact

`amends adr:neo-identity-source-of-truth-model` (§2.3, the lead cluster's placement: `neomjs/neo`'s README leads with the repository's own product and names the institution in its second sentence; the lead cluster opens the README's second part. The apex, the label, the ladder sentence and the other surfaces are unchanged). The placement of 2026-10-16 was the operator's, so his merge is the confirmation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1 **Look.** GitHub's render of the branch at 1440 × 900 shows on the README's first screen the title, both sentences, the record line, the three rows of doors and the upper part of the DevIndex picture; the six covers follow on the second screen. The pull request carries the first screen, the second screen and the whole page, as released and as changed.
- [ ] AC-2 **Cold look.** One reader without session context reads the changed first screen as a web engineer who followed an Engine 14 link and as a CTO who followed a link about the AI maintainers, and grades "what do I get, what do I do next" for each, with today's README as a blind control: above the control for both visitors in every round, and every gap to 9 of 10 named with its fate in the pull request. The prompt and all grades are in the pull request. The operator's glance at the pair is the density check before merge, because a model reads a wall without effort. *(Reworded on 20 Nov after four rounds. The first wording asked for 9 of 10 outright, written before any look existed; the rounds gave 7 to 8 and 6 to 7, 8 and 7 on the head, and two readers place the CTO's 9 beyond what a README can do alone.)*
- [ ] AC-3 The label, the ladder sentence and the apex paragraphs stand in the README word for word, except the dated proof line.
- [ ] AC-4 Each of the six covers and each group in the list links to `https://neomjs.com/#/examples/<group>` with a route from `MainContainer.mjs`; `npm run check-relative-links` passes.
- [ ] AC-5 `AudienceDoors.spec.mjs` asserts the README's new heading and passes.
- [ ] AC-6 ADR 0018 carries the §2.3 sentence and the 2026-11-20 entry in its Amended row.
- [ ] AC-7 The review is cross-family (`neo-identity-update`, step 4).
- [ ] AC-8 The pull request lists the out-of-tree change, the repository's description before and after, and who applies it.

## Post-Merge Validation

- [ ] After the release deploy: the six cover links and the list's group links open their group pages on neomjs.com in a browser.
- [ ] After the v14 publish: npm's package page shows the new first screen with its covers.
- [ ] The repository's description reads the Engine's projection.
- [ ] Fri 4 Dec: the stars of the 14 days after the merge against the 9 of the 14 days before it, read from the stargazer dates.

## Out of Scope

- **Shortening the sections below the second screen.** The page stays about ten screens long; that read comes after the cut.
- **The class count.** "461 classes across 39 namespaces" is stale (503 and 44 on this commit) in eight places, two of them outside this file's reach; it is noted as a defect (A2A `c90d3e10`, 20 Nov) and needs one source, not a ninth edit.
- **An org profile README.** `neomjs/.github` does not exist. It is the natural home of the whole, and a new repository is the operator's to create.
- The ladder sentence, the Portal's head, hero and doors, and `llms.txt`.
- A composed hero image or a v14 film cover.
- The READMEs of `neo-agent-brain` and `neo-agent-institution`.

## Avoided Traps

- **The label on top of this page.** This ticket's first shape kept it there, to leave the placement of 16 Oct alone. Two blind reads with today's README as the control graded that top 5 and 6 of 10 (a web engineer, a CTO) and the engine-first top 8 and 7; the label-first reader asked "is this a UI product or an AI experiment?". The ticket follows the reads, and the placement goes to the operator with them.
- **New screenshots.** The covers exist and are retaken with their examples; the README links them.
- **Example pages as link targets.** Half of the six do not exist on the live site before Monday; a group route degrades to the examples section.
- **Find and replace on "Body".** The team's section keeps the two-hemisphere vocabulary; only the first two screens say "engine".
